newsitem.title: USA: Decision on more USDA aid to Dakotas seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Decision on more USDA aid to Dakotas seen soon.

text.p: The Agriculture Department is likely to make an announcement soon on further assistance to weather-stricken ranchers and producers in the Dakotas, agency sources said Tuesday.

Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman met Monday with other USDA officials to discuss the weather crisis in North and South Dakota that has killed thousands of heads of livestock and threatens thousands more. Officials said ways to provide more help to beleaguered farmers and ranchers, within existing programs, were discussed and that a decision on USDA's next move would be made soon, probably by week's end.
"We are looking at the programs available to see what else we can do," said an official.
"We're obviously very sympathetic to their plight," said USDA press secretary Tom Amontree.

Glickman has been urged by Senators Byron Dorgan (D-ND) and Tom Daschle (D-SD) to provide more aid to the region. Glickman and Dorgan will be meeting later today on Capitol Hill to discuss the situation.
Deputy Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger will be travelling to the Dakotas on Friday for a first-hand look.

Severe cold temperatures and record snowfall since November have trapped thousands of cattle, sheep and other livestock without feed supplies. Unofficial estimates are that anywhere from 50,000 to 100,000 head of cattle have already perished and that this number could triple by winter's end.

USDA officials said that a complicating factor in the current situation is that the federal government no longer has the disaster programs in place that it did in the past, thereby limiting its ability to provide emergency assistance.
"Congress is going to have to step in at some point," said a USDA official.
